first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and is supported by two prior durable activation signals. Promotional pricing is tempting given competitor pressure, but inherited evidence indicates a material 30-day retention cost, conflicting with sustainable qualified revenue. Verify the primary onboarding result and the pricing downside before committing. Measure qualified activation and retain downstream retention and revenue guardrails because onboarding completion is only an upstream proxy.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior produced +13% completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention, directly addressing the current onboarding and activation declines while supporting sustainable revenue. Do not pursue promotional pricing: although it lifted qualified revenue 18%, verified 30-day retention fell 12% and the cohort failed to survive first renewal. Track completion, time-to-value, qualified activation, 30-day retention, and qualified revenue.

final2.rationale: Continue with onboarding simplification. Verified evidence shows +13% completion, 2.1-day faster time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue. The competitor’s deeper cut raises urgency but does not overturn the verified finding that a 40% SMB discount caused 12% lower 30-day retention and failed by first renewal. It is also unproven as a churn-save tactic. Track qualified activation, retention, revenue, and price-related churn; reassess pricing next cycle when verification is available.
